csv_project_name: Engineering Service 61st Avenue NE Sidewalk Replacement PH2
csv_scope_of_work: The City of Kenmore is requesting Statements of Qualifications (SOQ) from interested and qualified engineering firms to complete the following capital project by providing professional engineering services that may include (but not limited to): design, survey, geotechnical testing and evaluation, subsurface utility exploration, PS&E development, traffic engineering and analysis, surface water low impact design, wall design, utility coordination and design, permitting, right of way acquisition, environmental review (SEPA and NEPA) and documentation, critical area delineation, arborist review, cultural resources review, public outreach, engineering services during construction, grant applications and Council reports/updates. The City encourages disadvantaged, minority, women-owned, small business owned consultant firms (or teams) to respond The 61st AVE NE project will remove existing sidewalk on the east side of 61st AVE NE and relocate to the northbound lane.
csv_disciplines_requested: Civil Engineering, Geotechnical Engineering, Soil Testing, Surveying/GIS/Mapping, Planning/Master Planning, Sanitation Engineering, Archaeology, Forestry, Hydrology/Hydraulics, Stormwater, Traffic Design Engineering

title: Engineering Services for 61st Avenue NE Sidewalk Replacement Phase 2
short_description: Engineering services for sidewalk relocation and corridor improvements along 61st Avenue NE in Kenmore.
project_scope: Sidewalk replacement project on 61st Avenue NE in Kenmore. The existing sidewalk on the east side of 61st Avenue NE will be removed and relocated into the northbound lane. The project includes associated corridor and utility-related improvements, traffic considerations, surface water low impact design, wall design, permitting, right-of-way acquisition, environmental documentation, and construction-phase support. Total construction cost is stated as 4.4 million.
services: Professional engineering services including design, survey, geotechnical testing and evaluation, subsurface utility exploration, PS&E development, traffic engineering and analysis, surface water low impact design, wall design, utility coordination and design, permitting, right-of-way acquisition, environmental review and documentation under SEPA and NEPA, critical area delineation, arborist review, cultural resources review, public outreach, engineering services during construction, grant applications, and council reports/updates.
relevance_explanation:
- Primarily a sidewalk and streetscape/corridor project, not a bridge or special structure.
- Scope is dominated by civil, traffic, utility, environmental, and permitting services.
- No indication of complex structural engineering, long spans, lightweight structures, or architecturally demanding elements.
- Includes wall design, but no meaningful structural complexity is described.
- Fits poorly with sbp's core focus on bridges, long-span roofs, special structures, and complex building structures.
fee_explanation: No explicit fee information is provided. The notice states a total construction cost of 4.4 million USD and requests multidisciplinary engineering services, but no consultant fee or percentage is stated.
references_qualifications: Statements of Qualifications are requested from interested and qualified engineering firms. Specific minimum reference counts or detailed qualification thresholds are not stated in the provided text.

notes: Project number: 26-C3235. Target market: Streets/Highways. Federal funding is indicated. Questions deadline: 08/05/2026 05:00 PM EDT.
